statement: A finite algebraic cover of the complement of the identity in a nonabelian simple group produces an explicit unsolvable one-variable exponent-one equation. Every countably infinite group satisfying finite avoidance of all word zero sets that miss the identity admits an explicitly constructed nondiscrete Hausdorff metrizable group topology. Consequently every countable nonabelian simple group solving all one-variable unimodular equations, including every surviving simple countable quotient of the A.28 S2 example, is topologizable.
depends_on: Explicit finite word avoidance and weighted metric construction
A.28 only for the application to its quotients
manuscript_pages_settled: INDLOCAL A3(iii): further exact restriction on the remaining fixed-S2 countable-target case
notes: Full proof independently audited by root and C collaborator. No Markov or KOO theorem is used as an unproved input. The metric is explicitly separated by L(f_j)>=2^-j and conjugation satisfies L(khk^-1)<=D_k L(h). No completeness, compactness, or countable-system nonsolvability is inferred from the topology alone.
